diseases.scientificName: Plant nutritional disorder (specific nutrient and causal factor undetermined)
diseases.notes: User-contributed field lead expanded from grapevine to trees generally. Nutrient deficiency can affect many tree crops, including fruit trees, but visible patterns and susceptibility vary by species and cultivar. Yellowing is a symptom, not a nutrient diagnosis. Nitrogen deficiency often causes more uniform paling of older leaves; iron or manganese deficiency may cause interveinal chlorosis on young leaves; magnesium and potassium patterns often begin on older foliage, but patterns vary by crop. Similar symptoms can result from unsuitable soil pH, salinity, waterlogging/drought, root injury or disease, and nutrient excess or imbalance. Do not diagnose a specific element or recommend fertilizer from a photograph alone. Use crop-specific interpretation with soil and/or leaf-tissue analysis and field context.

diseases.notes: User-contributed field lead; location and season were not specified. Larvae mine within young expanding leaves, creating narrow serpentine/silvery galleries, often with a visible frass line; leaves may curl or become distorted. Chlorosis can occur in damaged tissue. Diagnose from the characteristic winding mine rather than yellowing alone. The pest attacks citrus generally, including lemon.

diseases.scientificName: Venturia oleaginea (syn. Spilocaea oleagina; anamorph name)
diseases.notes: User-contributed field lead; location, cultivar, season, specimen and expert confirmation were not specified. Typical symptoms are circular brown/olive-green to gray or dark spots, often with concentric rings and a yellow halo, mainly on the upper leaf surface. Severe/recurrent infection can cause chlorosis and premature leaf fall, especially in humid lower canopy. Infection is favored by prolonged leaf wetness, rain/high humidity and mild temperatures. Some infections may remain latent for months; absence of visible spots does not exclude infection. Do not diagnose from yellowing alone; microscopy or suitable laboratory testing can confirm.

diseases.applicability: User reports this symptom on walnut (Juglans spp.) and loquat (Eriobotrya japonica). Treat these host associations as field leads, not independently confirmed host-specific diagnoses. Interpret separately for each crop.
diseases.notes: User-described symptom: leaf margins and tips dry, turn brown and become brittle, sometimes progressing inward. This is marginal leaf necrosis/leaf scorch, a symptom pattern rather than one disease. Differential causes include drought or inadequate water uptake, hot/drying wind and heat, salinity or fertilizer-salt injury, unsuitable nutrient status, waterlogging/root injury or root rot, and some vascular pathogens. Loquat references list water deficit/excess, salinity and nutrient/mineral disorders among environmental problems; this does not establish a single cause. Walnut blight more typically causes small dark-brown spots with yellowish-green halos on leaves and can affect other green tissues; do not equate it with uniform marginal scorch. Compare distribution across canopy and trees, recent weather/irrigation/fertilizer/spray history, root-zone drainage, and presence of spots/lesions or branch dieback. Do not diagnose Xylella or any pathogen from marginal browning alone; pathogen confirmation requires appropriate laboratory testing. No treatment or fertilizer recommendation from a photograph alone.

diseases.notes: A crop-specific reference for citrus scab, especially relevant to lemon. Typical symptoms include small elevated pale-orange to pink/gray lesions that become raised, corky, wart-like protuberances on leaves and fruit; young leaves may become distorted and severely affected young fruit may be misshapen. This record is not evidence of current occurrence in Syria or any particular orchard. Distinguish sour citrus scab caused by E. fawcettii from sweet orange scab caused by E. australis; laboratory or qualified plant-health assessment may be needed for uncertain cases. No image labels or local prevalence claims are inferred.

datasets.intendedUse: Candidate for research; inspect annotation format, provenance and class balance before training.
datasets.notes: Original HERMOS publication reports 492 images and 13,913 Pascal VOC annotations from western Anatolia, Turkey. A 2026 CC BY 4.0 study reports retaining 491 source images and 13,765 regions after its own audit/filtering. Treat 491/13,765 as the independently reported filtered subset in that study, not necessarily a replacement official release count. Audit the downloaded version, labels, duplicates, and archive before training. Important count discrepancy: the Mendeley V2 landing page currently displays 914 images/13,904 labels, whereas the original 2022 paper states 492 images/13,913 labels and the 2026 audit found 492 image/XML pairs, 13,904 parsed objects, 13,765 usable regions, and 491 retained source images. These figures are not interchangeable; inspect the actual downloaded archive before using any count or manifest. A standard-library audit utility is now available at scripts/audit-hermos.py to generate a SHA-256 image manifest and check Pascal VOC pairing, object counts, bounding boxes, orphan XML files, and exact duplicates after the exact archive is downloaded. It does not establish label correctness, near-duplicates, provenance, or leakage-safe grouping. Current archive has not yet been downloaded or inspected; no training has occurred.

datasets.notes: Zenodo API confirms CC BY 4.0; archive 201,804,611 bytes verified against official MD5 3bf223ea8d83ce8ca73ef59585d61b12. Inventory: 555 readable images, 555 unique SHA-256, no internal exact duplicates, no exact SHA overlap with local PlantVillage full v2, Lemon V3, Citrus Field V3, Multi-Fruit original, Plasmopara original, or Citrus Zenodo v1. DCT pHash at Hamming <=8 found no pairs. However the archive does not map each image to its upstream source (ESCA-dataset, PlantDoc-Dataset, Grape Disease) and has no plant/vine/site/session IDs. EXIF shows strong class/source confounding: Healthy EXIF records are all dated 2025-07-04 (86); Leaf_blight 148/151 EXIF records are dated 2024-10-27; Esca 0/200 images retain EXIF; Black_rot records have mixed dates/devices. Therefore no diagnostic training until per-image source mapping, independent group metadata, and expert label review are resolved.

The depositor describes expert review and removal of duplicates/unclear images, but Mendeley states it does not curate dataset contents; these claims require archive-level and expert verification. Mendeley record lists CC BY 4.0; preserve creator attribution and citation. No archive has been downloaded or independently audited. Bangladesh data are not Syrian coastal validation.

classes: 125 cultivar names in the French-origin subset
14 cultivars used in the first morphology pilot
datasets.intendedUse: Controlled-image reference for grape-leaf morphology and an experimental cultivar-similarity feature only; not for plant-disease classification or diagnosis.
datasets.notes: The French-origin subset contains 504 readable images from 272 vine-position groups and 125 cultivar names. The first supervised morphology pilot used 127 images from 63 vine groups across 14 cultivars, with 3-fold StratifiedGroupKFold by block-row-vine. Mean grouped CV: accuracy 71.72%, balanced accuracy 70.44%, macro-F1 66.23%, top-3 accuracy 84.29%. Images were captured under controlled light-box/backlit conditions at the USDA Wolfskill repository in California, not in Syrian vineyards. The source has no disease labels; the model is experimental, not field validated, and must not be activated as a disease diagnostic model. Model artifact: DrPlant-Vitis-French-Morphology-Model-2026-11-24-v1.zip in Google Drive. Audit and metrics are retained in data/vitis-morphology/.

datasets.intendedUse: Research-only binary baseline; not for field diagnosis or application integration.
datasets.notes: Source metadata declares CC BY 4.0 and open access. Archive claims 281 originals; 280 extracted (129 Disease, 151 Healthy) plus 1,600 augmented derivatives. Only 280 originals were used; all are SHA-256 unique, no exact duplicates, no pHash pairs at Hamming <=8, and no exact SHA overlap with previously trained manifests checked. Stratified image-level split 196/42/42; no plant/vine/site/session IDs. Eight-epoch MobileNetV3-Small baseline: validation accuracy 88.10%, test accuracy 73.81%, test macro-F1 73.79%. Test set only 42 images. Labels not independently expert-reviewed. Research-only; no production integration or treatment use.
